example.prompt: Compare the pure fertiliser solutes using only this supplied table. Ammonia, NH3: 82.4% nitrogen by mass, gas at room conditions, alkaline aqueous solution. Ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3: 35.0% nitrogen by mass, soluble solid granules, near-neutral aqueous solution. Select two supported advantages and two disadvantages. example.answer: Pure ammonia has the higher nitrogen mass fraction but is a gas and its aqueous solution is alkaline, complicating handling and risking pH change. Award one linked point for under-adding acid and explaining that more hydroxide remains before equivalence, causing a higher bulk conductivity. “Not stirred” is disabled because its bias direction depends on probe location; generic “human error” scores zero.
source_brief.feedback: After submission, name the first missing or incompatible credited element and show the complete example-specific response; do not reveal answers before submission.
variations: Change the named substances or readings while preserving the same apparatus purpose and assessed causal link.
constraints: The activity must state acid is added to alkali, all readings are before equivalence, and conductivity represents a thoroughly mixed bulk sample.

source_brief.objective: Complete the assessed operation deterministically: explain group 7 reactivity trend.
source_brief.interaction: A finite clause builder: the learner selects or completes separate subject, comparison, cause and consequence fields in required order.
source_brief.activity_fit: Proposed chemistry clause-builder activity with deterministic controls.
source_brief.answer_representation: An ordered array of independently markable propositions with typed entities and directed relationships.
source_brief.marking: Four linked fields: iodine has more occupied shells/greater distance; greater shielding; weaker nuclear attraction for an incoming electron; iodine gains it less readily and is less reactive. A fully consistent reverse chlorine comparison is equivalent; electron-loss reasoning is rejected. Example target: Iodine has more occupied shells, so an incoming electron is farther from and more shielded from the nucleus, feels weaker attraction, and is gained less readily.
source_brief.feedback: Highlight the first missing proposition or broken causal link and contrast it with the learner’s selected relationship.
variations: Vary the halogen pair and require the comparative shell/distance, shielding, attraction and incoming-electron-gain chain.
constraints: All prompts are self-contained; anything not assessed is supplied and locked.
Use finite parsed responses only: no AI marking, self-marking or broad substring matching.
misconceptions: Reversing the Group 7 trend, confusing halogen elements with halide ions, or treating astatine predictions as measured bulk data.

example.answer: Iodine has more occupied shells, so an incoming electron is farther from and more shielded from the nucleus, feels weaker attraction, and is gained less readily.

variations: Vary the halogen pair and activate either the seven-outer-electron similarity module or the distance–shielding–attraction–electron-gain trend module.
constraints: All prompts are self-contained; anything not assessed is supplied and locked.
Use finite parsed responses only: no AI marking, self-marking or broad substring matching.
misconceptions: Reversing the Group 7 trend, confusing halogen elements with halide ions, or treating astatine predictions as measured bulk data.

source_brief.marking: Credit five ordered stages in the example: gentle partial evaporation to near saturation; cooling to crystallise; filtration; a little cold distilled-water wash; drying. 2019-june-1-q14e requirement: Heat/boil the filtrate to evaporate some water.
2019-june-1-q14e requirement: Continue until a cooled sample or glass rod forms crystals, or until the crystallisation point/saturation is reached.
2019-june-1-q14e requirement: Leave the concentrated solution to cool and crystallise.
2019-june-1-q14e requirement: Filter or decant to separate the crystals.
2019-june-1-q14e requirement: Dry the crystals with filter paper/paper towel, in a warm oven, in a desiccator, or by leaving them to dry.

2019-june-1-q14e marking rule: The saturation/crystallisation-point mark depends on prior heating. Heating to dryness allows only the heating mark; leaving the unheated solution to evaporate all water allows only one mark. Complete evaporation after heating caps the response at three. Washing is ignored. Reject a hot oven or direct heating; no drying mark if crystals are washed after drying.

2019-june-1r-q7aii requirement: For the solution stage, award any three: warm the acid without boiling; add magnesium oxide little by little until excess remains/no more dissolves; stir; filter off excess solid.
2019-june-1r-q7aii requirement: For crystallisation, heat the filtrate to remove some water until saturated/crystallisation point.
2019-june-1r-q7aii requirement: Allow to cool and crystallise, separate the crystals by filtration or decanting, and dry with filter paper, a warm oven or desiccator.

2019-june-1r-q7aii marking rule: Award any three from each stage. If excess oxide is added but not filtered off, cap the crystallisation stage at two. Do not credit a hot oven/direct heating for drying; drying depends on separating crystals first, and washing after drying cancels that point. Within the second stage, heating and reaching crystallisation point are separate source points; the crystallisation-point point depends on heating.
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Compulsory: warm or heat the nitric acid without boiling.
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Compulsory: add, mix or react red lead oxide and stir.

2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Isolation: heat the filtrate (one available mark).
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Isolation: reach crystallisation point or a saturated solution; the MS also allows removing some water (one available mark, dependent on heating).
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Isolation: leave to cool or form more crystals (one available mark).
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Isolation: filter or decant to separate crystals (one available mark, dependent on cooling).
2020-nov-1-q10cii requirement: Isolation: dry between filter papers, with paper towel, in a warm oven or by leaving to dry (one available mark).

2020-nov-1-q10cii marking rule: All three compulsory points and any three isolation points earn six. Heating to dryness earns only the heating point. Crystallisation-point credit depends on heating; filtering crystals depends on cooling. Washing is ignored. Direct heating or a hot oven is rejected for drying, and drying earns no mark if washing is placed after it. The MS ignores adding excess red lead oxide; that historical exception is retained only here and is not proposed as a general preparation rule.

2022-june-1-q3bii requirement: Alkenes are needed or used to make polymers or plastics.

2022-june-1-q3bii marking rule: Award any two. Merely saying shorter-chain alkanes are fuels is insufficient. A generic statement that shorter products are more useful/in demand/more flammable, or that cracking creates shorter alkanes and alkenes, scores one only if no other mark is awarded.
